-_plan_cache = _merge_plan.cache

+@_memo
+def _get_decoder(n2: int, base: int):
+    # Specialise the merge plan for (n2, base) into straight-line code, so a
+    # decode runs its rounds without loop, tuple-unpacking and lookup work.
+    sub, plan, s, tail = _merge_plan(n2, base)
+    t = (base & -base).bit_length() - 1
+    # In the final round (two lanes, no dense tail) the high mask is an
+    # identity when the low lane cannot reach the shifted bits.
+    free = not tail and base < (1 << (8 - t))
+    last = len(sub) + len(plan)
+    ns = {'_dense_tail': _dense_tail}
+    body = []
+    i = 0
+    for shift, mask, c in sub:
+        i += 1
+        ns['c%d' % i] = c
+        if free and i == last:
+            body.append('x -= (x >> %d) * c%d' % (shift, i))
+        else:
+            ns['h%d' % i] = mask
+            body.append('x -= (x >> %d & h%d) * c%d' % (shift, i, i))
+    for shift, hmask, mult, mask in plan:
+        i += 1
+        ns['c%d' % i] = mult
+        ns['m%d' % i] = mask
+        if free and i == last:
+            body.append('x = (x >> %d) * c%d + (x & m%d)' % (shift, i, i))
+        else:
+            ns['h%d' % i] = hmask
+            body.append('x = (x >> %d & h%d) * c%d + (x & m%d)'
+                        % (shift, i, i, i))
+    if tail:
+        ns['T'] = tail
+        body.append('return _dense_tail(x, %d, T)' % s)
+    else:
+        body.append('return x')
+    params = ''.join(', %s=%s' % (k, k) for k in ns if k != '_dense_tail')
+    src = 'def f(x%s):\n    %s\n' % (params, '\n    '.join(body))
+    exec(src, ns)
+    return ns['f']
+
+
+_plan_cache = _merge_plan.cache
+_dec_cache = _get_decoder.cache
+_table_cache = _get_decode_table.cache

actions.reason: Decode merge plans are now specialised per (padded length, base) into straight-line functions, built once with exec and memoised. Constants are bound as default arguments, and int.from_bytes runs inside the generated function. This removes the per-round loop, tuple unpacking and global lookups on every decode. In the final two-lane round with no dense tail, the high mask is dropped when base < 2**(8-t). Under that condition the low lane can never reach the shifted bits, so the mask does nothing there. b58decode also reuses newlen instead of calling len(digits). Outputs are identical. decode_autofix_ir ratio is 0.9830; the other metrics stay within guard limits.

journal.text:
I tried speeding up decode_autofix_ir in base58/__init__.py. The approach was to specialise decode merge plans per (padded length, base) into straight-line functions, built once with exec and memoised. Constants are bound as default arguments, and int.from_bytes runs inside the generated function. That removes the per-round loop, tuple unpacking and global lookups.

My first two sandbox runs were rejected for no improvement. They reached ratios of 0.9913 and 0.9923 against the required 0.9900. The third, at 67 changed lines, was accepted with decode_autofix_ir at ratio 0.9830. Outputs were identical every time. Other metrics drifted up slightly but stayed within guard limits, for example decode_long_ir at 1.0070. I submitted it and it is queued for replay, with no verdict yet.

I believe the margin here is thin and the codegen path helps the target while costing the other decode paths a little.

Next I would look at why decode_long_ir and int_codec_ir rose, and whether those paths can share the generated functions.
